title: Standardize mesh-node socket naming and port-type conventions
description:
The current 82-node catalog (ixdar-app/target/mesh-node-catalog.json) has several naming inconsistencies that confuse both humans and LLM agents, directly causing agent-loop failures in voyage runs (Apr 2026 skull run livelocked for 60 min because Gemma kept writing .geometry on primitives, which output .mesh).

## Empirical findings from a full-catalog audit (see voyage/batch.py feedback injection for motivation)

### 1) Same port TYPE, divergent output NAMES (visible agent confusion)

- GEOMETRY_BUNDLE outputs use 7 different names: geometry (35×), curve (5×), selected (1×), inverted (1×), iso_curve (1×), boundary_a (1×), boundary_b (1×). The 'curve' split is the biggest offender: circle_curve/curve_bezier/join_curves/mesh_to_curve/resample_curve all output a GEOMETRY_BUNDLE but name it 'curve', while every other node naming a GEOMETRY_BUNDLE output calls it 'geometry'.
- VECTOR3 outputs use 9 different names: vector (5×), plus tangent, vector_out, attach_position, attach_normal, attach_rotation, result, min, max.
- FLOAT outputs use 12 different names: result (6×), index (2×), float_out (1×), plus single-use ones (total_cost, value, x, y, z, end_rx, end_ry, end_tx, end_ty).
- BOOLEAN outputs use 3 different names: selection (3× — selection primitives), generated (4× — inset/extrude), result (3× — boolean math). Arguably semantically justified but worth a naming convention.

### 2) Same output NAME, divergent port TYPES

- 'result' is used for FLOAT (6×), INT (3×), BOOLEAN (3×), VECTOR3 (1×). The agent has no way to predict the type without node-specific lookup.

### 3) Dual (overlapping) output pattern

Several modifier / surface nodes expose BOTH  and  as outputs of the same operation (extrude_mesh, inset_faces, loop_cut, subdivide_mesh, subdivision_surface, solidify_mesh, coons_extrude_mesh, coons_inset_faces). Agents aren't told which to chain; picking 'mesh' on a cage-level op drops handle metadata silently. The 'generated:BOOLEAN' co-output (inset/extrude/coons_*) is great but poorly advertised.

### 4) Dual INPUT ports for the same concept

loop_cut, subdivision_surface accept BOTH  and  as inputs — the agent (correctly!) interpreted this as 'I should pass both', then failed because only one is actually consumed. Undocumented aliasing.

### 5) Primitive naming conflict

, , :
- 'sphere' and 'uv_sphere' are both spheres; sphere uses 'size' instead of 'radius'. Naming collision with uv_sphere's meaning, different size/radius parameter name for the same concept.

### 6) Dropped/orphan outputs

 returns 4 GEOMETRY_BUNDLE outputs (geometry, iso_curve, boundary_a, boundary_b) — all the same type.  returns 2 (selected, inverted).  returns 4 outputs including 3 VECTOR3 auxiliaries. These break the 'one primary output' convention and need a named-tuple / bundle story in the docs.

## Proposed standards (to land in .cursor/docs/ai-learnings/ and enforce in annotation processor)

1. One primary output name per port type:
   - MESH → 
   - GEOMETRY_BUNDLE →  (rename 'curve' outputs on curve-producing nodes; OR introduce a CURVE port type distinct from GEOMETRY_BUNDLE and separately standardize)
   - BOOLEAN selection → 
   - BOOLEAN produced-this-operation → 
   - BOOLEAN/FLOAT/INT scalar computation → 
   - VECTOR3 standalone → 
   - ROTATION → 
   - CLOSURE → 

2. 'result' pinned to FLOAT. Rename boolean_math.result → value (or bool_out), integer_math.result → int_value, switch_vector.result → vector. Same name = same type everywhere.

3. Dual mesh/geometry output on modifier nodes: document which to chain and when. Proposal: keep both, but annotation-processor adds a canonical-next-hop hint ('prefer .geometry when chaining into cage ops; prefer .mesh for terminal GPU submission').

4. Dual mesh/geometry INPUT ports: deprecate one. Either (a) collapse to  only (wrap MESH in a zero-cost bundle), or (b) keep as aliases but document explicitly in _format_node_summary so the prompt/catalog says '(accepts either mesh OR geometry)'.

5. Primitive uniformity:
   - Rename  →  (if its semantics differ from uv_sphere) or merge.
   - Standardize sizing parameter to  across all sphere variants; keep __TEXT	__DATA	__OBJC	others	dec	hex only for cube/grid where it semantically differs.

6. Catalog export (MeshNodeCatalog.toJson) should include a 'canonical_chain_output' field per node — the annotation processor already has enough info to pick one of the outputs as the 'default chaining output'. This flows through mesh-node-catalog.json → build_mesh_system_prompt() and removes an entire class of agent confusion without re-teaching.

## Why this matters now

Daud's voyage runs on Gemma 4 31B are spending whole 60-minute member budgets on port-name confusion. We just landed a feedback-injection patch (voyage/batch.py; file:line ~394 _maybe_checkpoint, ~627 _visual_round_callback) that surfaces validator errors into the agent's next turn, which recovers the loop. But the root cause — a catalog that's internally inconsistent — is still there. Fixing the catalog reduces errors to fix, tightens the agent loop, and improves human readability of .dsl files.

## Shell-quoting corrections to the description above

Several identifier literals got dropped by zsh backtick-expansion when this ticket was filed. Here are the lost fragments, in order of appearance:

Section 3 (Dual output pattern) should read: Several modifier / surface nodes expose BOTH mesh:MESH and geometry:GEOMETRY_BUNDLE as outputs of the same operation.

Section 4 (Dual INPUT ports) should read: loop_cut and subdivision_surface accept BOTH mesh:MESH and geometry:GEOMETRY_BUNDLE as inputs.

Section 5 (Primitive naming conflict) should read: Three sphere variants coexist — sphere(size:FLOAT, resolution:INT), uv_sphere(radius:FLOAT, segments:INT, rings:INT), icosphere(radius:FLOAT, subdivisions:INT). sphere and uv_sphere are both spheres; sphere uses size instead of radius. Naming collision with uv_spheres meaning, different size/radius parameter name for the same concept.

Section 6 (Dropped/orphan outputs) should read: bi_rail_loft returns 4 GEOMETRY_BUNDLE outputs (geometry, iso_curve, boundary_a, boundary_b) — all the same type. separate_geometry returns 2 (selected, inverted). attach_to_surface returns 4 outputs including 3 VECTOR3 auxiliaries.

Proposed standards section 1 (One primary output name per port type):
- MESH => mesh
- GEOMETRY_BUNDLE => geometry
- BOOLEAN selection => selection
- BOOLEAN produced-this-operation => generated
- BOOLEAN/FLOAT/INT scalar computation => result
- VECTOR3 standalone => vector
- ROTATION => rotation
- CLOSURE => closure

Proposed standards section 4 (Dual mesh/geometry INPUT ports) should read: deprecate one. Either (a) collapse to geometry only (wrap MESH in a zero-cost bundle), or (b) keep as aliases but document explicitly in _format_node_summary so the prompt/catalog says (accepts either mesh OR geometry).

Proposed standards section 5 (Primitive uniformity):
- Rename sphere => sdf_sphere (if its semantics differ from uv_sphere) or merge with uv_sphere.
- Standardize sizing parameter to radius across all sphere variants; keep size only for cube/grid where it semantically differs.

## 2026-04-18 scope decision

Not in prod yet. Skipping the deprecation-alias layer entirely — old .dsl files under ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/ will break and get updated in the same PR. This drops the DoD item about '.dsl files keep validating with a warning' and simplifies the annotation-processor change (just enforce canonical names; no alias plumbing).

Simplified DoD:
1. Canonical-name table defined in annotations module (one output name per port type).
2. Annotation processor FAILS the build on non-canonical output names (no @NonStandardOutputName escape hatch for this first pass — we can add one later if a legitimate exception shows up).
3. All nodes renamed in-place to canonical names.
4. All existing .dsl files in ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/ updated to match and still validate.
5. Catalog JSON regenerates cleanly; audit script shows zero inconsistencies after.
6. Daud's mesh_context._format_node_summary surfaces the cleaner schema automatically (no Daud-side change needed — it just reads the updated catalog).
definition-of-done: 1. Audit report lands at .cursor/docs/ai-learnings/mesh-node-socket-conventions.md with the empirical inconsistency tables (same-type-different-name; same-name-different-type; dual-mesh/geometry; primitive naming). 2. Annotation-processor validation pass (fails the build) for: output names must match the canonical-name table for their port type, except when explicitly marked with @NonStandardOutputName; no two nodes share an output name with different port types. 3. Proposed renames applied behind a deprecation alias layer so existing .dsl files continue to validate (emit deprecation warning in validator output). 4. MeshNodeCatalog.toJson exports a 'canonical_chain_output' field per node, consumed by daud.mesh_context._format_node_summary (Daud repo; follow-up can be a separate ticket). 5. Ixdar validator's 'Valid outputs: X' error text already works (no change needed there); confirm it covers BOTH the canonical and deprecated alias outputs with a clear 'deprecated' tag. 6. All existing .dsl files in ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/ still validate (ran through the auto-validate pipeline).
testing-plan: 1. Run the audit script (a one-shot Python that reads mesh-node-catalog.json) before and after the rename pass — diff should show ALL inconsistencies gone. 2. Full mvn test on Ixdar. 3. Run every .dsl file in ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/ through the validator — expect 100% still-validate. 4. Kick off a Daud voyage run on the skull reference; compare tool_errors + validation_errors count per round against the current baseline (20260418-211601). Expect large drop in the first-round 'no output port X' class of errors. 5. Regression check: pyright on Daud's mesh_context.py after catalog format changes.
